"Perpendicular height from floor of the king’s to roof of Col. Campbell’s chamber — 69 ft 3 in", Appendix p. 112. This is the one figure that closes the stack: with the five chambers’ own heights and the King’s Chamber’s, it fixes how thick the granite floor beams between them are, which no source states.
The eleven sloping roof slabs "rested upon a low wall about three feet high, which allowed for the inequalities of the floor" (p. 277). Vyse writes "about", so the sigma is six inches.
"Passage leading to Davison’s chamber — length 24 ft 9 in", Appendix p. 112. Petrie §62 calls the rough passage "over 20 feet long", which agrees.
The pitched roof is "eleven slabs of calcareous stone, twelve feet three inches long" (p. 277), each slab spanning half the 20 ft 6 in width from the wall top to the ridge.

§62, p. 91, the table of "the actual dimensions of these chambers". Petrie adds on p. 92 that "these dimensions are merely of the rough masonry; and some lengths could not be measured owing to the encumbrance of blocks of stone and rubbish left in the chambers from Vyse’s excavations", so the sigma is his roughness, not his instrument. The "1st" row, N. column.

§62, p. 94: "In the fifth or top chamber, the width is quite undefined; and we can only say that between the points where the sloping roof-slabs appear is 247 inches." It is where the roof springs, not a wall, so it is not the chamber’s width; it is here because it agrees with Vyse’s 20 ft 6 in to within an inch and so checks him.

§62, p. 92: two vertical masons’ lines on the S. wall of the second chamber, 413.5 apart, "evidently intended for the length of the King’s Chamber below them, and define the required limits of this upper space". With the 204.65 mid-line pair on the E. wall it is why the chambers are drawn centred on the King’s Chamber.
§62, p. 92: on the E. wall of the second chamber a vertical mid-line, 101.8 to a line at the S. end and 102.85 to one at the N. end, "total, 204.65, intended for King’s Chamber width".
§62, p. 91: "The rough passage is 28½ wide, 32 inches high, and over 20 feet long", the passage from the top of the gallery’s east wall into Davison’s chamber.
